items.titleEn: Gold price at CAD$5,684/oz after Bank of Canada raises 25 bps, sees growth slowing in Q4 before rebounding in 2028
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The Bank of Canada (BoC) raised its key overnight rate to 2.50% on Wednesday, as expected, with the bank rate rising to 2.75% and the deposit rate rising to 2.45%. The BoC said the global economic activity has remained resilient despite higher energy prices. “In the United States, the economy continues to grow at a robust pace, supported by consumer spending and AI-related investment,” they said. “Growth in the euro area has been resilient and broad-based. After slowing in the second quarter, Chinese growth rebounded in the third quarter, owing to strength in exports and a pickup in fiscal spending.” “Given the ongoing resilience of the global economy, the Bank has revised up global GDP growth slightly to 3.1% in 2026, while growth in 2027 and 2028 remains unchanged from the July projection at 3.2%,” they added.

Gold recovery stalls as Saudi refinery attack claims lift crude, silver retreats - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were lower in early U.S. trading Wednesday, as renewed tensions involving Iran and its regional allies pushed crude oil prices higher and reinforced concerns about persistent inflation ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision. Gold surrendered part of Tuesday's recovery as traders assessed the possibility of additional monetary tightening in December, while silver remained under pressure amid concerns about industrial demand and elevated borrowing costs. Spot gold was trading near $4,054.60 an ounce, down $6.36, or 0.16%, while silver was near $54.202, down $0.195, or 0.40%. Market positioning remains focused on an expected Federal Reserve pause Wednesday, with traders assigning approximately an 84% probability to at least one additional interest rate increase by December. The combination of elevated yields, a firm dollar and persistent expectations for additional Fed tightening continues to limit gold's ability to attract sustained buying interest despite geopolitical uncertainty. The Federal Open Market Committee concludes its two-day meeting Wednesday, with the interest rate decision scheduled for 2 p.m. EDT, followed by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's news conference at 2:30 p.m. EDT. Policymakers are widely expected to leave the federal funds target range unchanged at 3.75% to 4.00%, shifting attention toward the accompanying statement and the chairman's assessment of inflation, employment and the possibility of another increase in December. Wednesday's remaining economic calendar includes the weekly Energy Information Administration petroleum inventory report at 10:30 a.m. EDT. Thursday brings the advance third-quarter gross domestic product estimate, September personal consumption expenditures inflation figures and weekly initial jobless claims, all scheduled for 8:30 a.m. EDT. Softer inflation readings or less restrictive Fed guidance could reduce December rate hike expectations and support gold through lower Treasury yields and a weaker dollar. Conversely, persistent price pressures and a hawkish policy message would reinforce expectations for additional tightening and maintain pressure on bullion.

Europe's digital dependence is rising—the U.S. and China pull ahead
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Dependence on digital technologies in the European Union continues to grow—despite all calls for greater digital sovereignty. Between 2010 and 2023, Europe's "Digital Dependence Index" (DDI) rose by 0.5 percentage points, while China reduced its dependence by nearly 11 percentage points and the U.S. by 6 percentage points. A major weakness lies in digital platforms, where European countries are almost entirely dependent on foreign providers. This is according to a policy study by the Vodafone Institute and the Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies (CASSIS) at the University of Bonn.
